overview: Spicy's Killaura is a compact 1.8 combat module driven from a single EventMotion pre handler, with EventRenderGUI reserved for an on-screen target HUD (health bar, HP readout and a rendered entity preview). Every tick it rebuilds the candidate list by streaming loadedEntityList through a distance filter and a Players/Animals/Mobs/Everything type filter, keeps the last target in Switch mode until switchTime expires, optionally prunes Hypixel 'watchdog bots' by tab-list responseTime, writes the aim into the outgoing movement packet (lock mode: exact yaw minus 2 degrees plus a triangular pitch oscillation; smooth mode: updateRotation easing capped at 180 degrees per tick), and attacks on a real millisecond timer whose period is 1000 / (APS + a fresh random float), so inter-hit intervals jitter. The attack packet itself is preceded by an arm swing (or a direct C0APacketAnimation when noSwing is set) and followed by client-side critical particles when the Criticals module is on and the player is grounded, and the Hypixel autoblock flavor re-blocks with a sendPacketNoEvent burst of C02 vector-interact, C02 INTERACT and a C08 block placement at BlockPos(-1, -1, -1) with facing 255.

sections.p: The EventMotion pre branch is the whole brain. It first toggles the module off when disableOnDeath and the player is dead, then clears the target and rebuilds the candidate list every tick: loadedEntityList entities that are EntityLivingBase are streamed, sorted by distance, filtered to the range setting (and to alive entities with health > 0 when dontHitDeadEntitys is on), then run through the targetsSetting type filter (players-only, animals-only, mobs-only or everything) via a targetsToRemove pass. When the list is empty the module resets the render rotations (RenderUtils.resetPlayerYaw/Pitch), stops blocking and returns. Otherwise target = targets.get(0), with Switch mode holding lastTarget while it is still in range and only re-picking to targets.get(0) once targetSwitchTimer.hasTimeElapsed(switchTime * 1000). The Hypixel antibot branch removes a targeted player whose netHandler responseTime is greater than 1 (their heuristic for a watchdog bot) and returns. A position-equality guard skips rotation entirely when the target occupies the player's own coordinates, which the source comment says avoids the 'invalid player movement' kick.

lock mode writes yaw = rotations[0] - 2 every tick and drives pitch with upAndDownPitch, a 20-tick triangular wave: each tick adds 2 + random, below 10 the pitch is rotations[1] - upAndDownPitch, between 10 and 20 it is rotations[1] + 10 - (upAndDownPitch - 10), and at 20 the accumulator resets, with a -90 clamp at the end. The effect is a sawtooth sweep of up to 20 degrees across the target's vertical angle, re-synced every 20 ticks -- a periodic, machine-regular pitch pattern. smooth mode runs customRots: sYaw = updateRotation(lastSmoothYaw, targetYaw, 180) and sPitch likewise, then re-converges with updateRotation(..., 360), clamping pitch to +-90; updateRotation wraps the delta with MathHelper.wrapAngleTo180_float and clamps it to the factor, so the per-tick yaw delta is bounded at 180 degrees but still reaches the target within one or two packets. The attack gate is a Timer, not a tick counter: timer.hasTimeElapsed((long)(1000 / (aps + new Random().nextFloat())), true), so the inter-hit interval at 10 APS averages ~95ms with +-1ms of random dither, and at 20 APS drops to ~48-50ms. hitOnHurtTime returns early while target.hurtTime > 2, and the Sprint module's state is re-asserted with setSprinting(true) both before and after the attack so the server never sees sprint drop mid-combat.

sections.h: Autoblock packet flow and target HUD
sections.p: startBlocking is called every tick a target exists and routes by mode: Vanilla uses playerController.sendUseItem (the real use-item path, so the server sees a genuine item-use begin), Hypixel uses blockHypixel, which sends three packets through sendPacketNoEvent (bypassing the event bus): a C02PacketUseEntity with Action.INTERACT and a Vec3 built from RotationUtils.getVectorForRotation(rotations[0], rotations[1]) -- the aim vector itself as the interact point -- a second C02 with Action.INTERACT, and a C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement at BlockPos(-1, -1, -1) with facing 255 and the held item. The negative-coordinate placement is the classic Hypixel sword-block spoof: the server treats it as blocking without a real block face. Before each attack stopBlocking sends a C07PacketPlayerDigging RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN and clears keyBindUseItem.pressed, and onDisable unwinds Hypixel blocking with onStoppedUsingItem inside a try/catch. The EventRenderGUI branch draws the target HUD: a health bar whose position lerps toward the target value at /5 per frame (healthBar += (target - healthBar) / 5), an HSB or rainbowgui-driven color, the target name, an HP line, and a live entity preview via GuiInventory.drawEntityOnScreen.

files.label: Killaura.java (module)
files.explanation:
The settings surface is declared as public fields: range (default 4, max 6), aps (default 10, max 20), noSwing, disableOnDeath, dontHitDeadEntitys, targetsSetting, rotationSetting (lock/smooth), newAutoblock (None/Vanilla/Hypixel), targetingMode (Single/Switch), switchTime (0.1-10s), and hitOnHurtTime. onEnable snapshots lastSmoothYaw/Pitch, seeds dynamicAPS and resets the pitch oscillator; onDisable resets the render rotations and unwinds a parked Hypixel block via keyBindUseItem.pressed = false + onStoppedUsingItem in a try/catch. The EventMotion pre branch (line 233) does all targeting: stream filter + distance sort, type filter, Switch-mode lastTarget retention, the Hypixel responseTime > 1 bot removal (which literally calls mc.theWorld.removeEntity on the 'bot'), the position-equality rotation guard, and then the attack block (line 462): stopBlocking, swing (C0A direct when noSwing, else swingItem), the C02 ATTACK, onEnchantmentCritical when sharpness applies, onCriticalHit when the Criticals module is enabled and the player is onGround (client-side particles only, no packet), sprint re-assert, and the Hypixel re-block.

The helpers carry the packet work: blockHypixel (line 525) emits the C02 vector-interact + C02 INTERACT + C08(-1,-1,-1) triple through sendPacketNoEvent; sendUseItem (line 540) replicates the vanilla use-item path (syncCurrentPlayItem + useItemRightClick); startBlocking (line 596) switches on mode and re-sends the use-item while already blocking; stopBlocking (line 575) sends C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN; customRots (line 673) and updateRotation (line 720) implement the 180-degree-capped easing. The HUD branch (line 158) lerps the health bar and draws the entity preview. The file also keeps two dead settings (autoblock, targetModeSetting) solely to migrate old configs, and its noSwing path proves the arm-animation packet is always emitted one way or the other.

files.label: RotationUtils.java (aim math)
files.explanation: This 65-line file is a direct port of old Sigma's RotationUtils -- the source comment says so verbatim ('FOUND ON THE OLD SIGMA SOURCE CODE' with a gitlab link) -- and it exposes exactly the geometry the module consumes. getRotations aims at ent.posY + ent.getEyeHeight() / 2.0F and getRotationFromPosition subtracts a fixed 1.2 from the player's Y, so the pitch is consistently biased low by a constant; getYawChange and getPitchChange return wrapped deltas with the same -2.5 degree bias baked into getPitchChange. getVectorForRotation is the standout: it converts a (pitch, yaw) pair into the unit Vec3 (sin/cos composition with -pitch * 0.017453292 radian scaling), which blockHypixel uses as the interact-point vector of the first C02 in its blocking burst -- the server receives an interact aimed exactly along the module's own aim line. Because the module shares this one file with its other combat modules, the same biased aim math shows up in every rotation-based feature, and the per-tick deltas the smooth/lock modes write to movement packets are all derived from this file's atan2 composition.

files.label: Timer.java (attack-rate gate)
files.explanation: A 27-line stopwatch: hasTimeElapsed(long time, boolean reset) returns true once System.currentTimeMillis() - lastMS exceeds the argument, optionally re-anchoring lastMS. Killaura uses two instances. The attack gate timer is polled every EventMotion pre tick with 1000 / (aps + new Random().nextFloat()) -- the per-call random float means the period itself jitters by up to 1ms per roll, so the inter-attack intervals at any fixed APS are not perfectly uniform (at 10 APS ~95ms nominal, at 20 APS ~48ms). The static targetSwitchTimer gates Switch-mode re-picking with switchTime * 1000. Because the gate is wall-clock and not tick-synchronized, the attack cadence drifts relative to the 50ms tick grid, which is the one timing fingerprint that distinguishes this module from tick-locked auras -- at 20 APS it can fire two attacks in adjacent ticks during a drift, which is what the per-second attack counters in anticheats catch.

countering.label: EntityInteractReach (interact reach)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's EntityInteractReach validates every entity-interaction packet (C02 with INTERACT or ATTACK) by measuring the distance from the attacker's head position to the victim's hitbox, lag-compensated to the attacker's ping, with MAX_REACH 3.1 and MAX_REACH_CREATIVE 5.0 (set in the constructor, both overrideable). The victim AABB comes from WrappedEntity.getWrappedEntity().getHitbox(victimLocation) and the attacker point from att.getHeadPosition(); a distance over the ceiling punishes, otherwise it rewards. It deliberately does not ray trace -- it is a pure distance-to-box check, which makes it the harshest possible form of reach enforcement for interact-heavy auras.

Spicy's Hypixel autoblock is a direct target: every blocking cycle emits two C02 packets against the target (the vector INTERACT from blockHypixel and the plain INTERACT), and at the module's range setting of 4-6 (default 4) every one of those interacts sits beyond 3.1 and flags, so simply having Hypixel autoblock enabled turns the module into a reach violation generator regardless of the attack rate. Plain attacks in the 3.2-6 range band flag identically. The bypass is to keep range at or under 3.1 and drop Hypixel autoblock -- both of which gut the module's purpose, since its own range ceiling of 6 exists precisely to hit from outside normal reach.

countering.label: Angle (fight.angle multi-target ledger)
countering.explanation:
NCP's fight Angle check keeps a 1-second window (maxTimeDiff = 1000ms) of attack locations and scores four averages over the window: avgmove (average distance between consecutive hits; below 0.2 blocks adds 20 * (0.2 - avgMove) / 0.2), avgtime (below 150ms adds 30 * (150 - avgTime) / 150), avgyaw (above 50 degrees adds 30 * avgYaw / 180) and switchspeed (each hit on a different entity with a yaw jump over 30 degrees adds 20 * avgSwitching). The largest term over its threshold fires; otherwise the VL decays by 0.98. The ledger is cleared whenever an entry ages out, so a player must sustain the pattern, not just spike once.

Spicy's Switch mode re-picks targets on a real-time timer (switchTime default 2s, minimum 0.1s) and lock mode snaps the yaw to the new target in one movement packet, so with two targets more than 30 degrees apart and a short switchTime the ledger fills with idDiffLast entries carrying yawDiffLast over 30 -- the switchspeed term runs at 20 per switch. Standing fights feed avgmove (attacks with no translation between hits) and the APS ceiling of 20 keeps hits ~50ms apart, so avgtime sits at a third of the 150ms bound and contributes ~20 per pair. At 20 APS + 0.1s switchTime all four terms accumulate simultaneously and the check cancels the hits before the window even fills. The mitigation that passes is the module's own default posture: 10 APS and 2s switching keeps avgtime near the bound and switchspeed sparse.

countering.label: KillAura (fight.killaura direction/reach/speed)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's KillAura check runs per combat event with defaults max-direction-angle 1.2 (radians), max-swing-time 80ms, max-reach 4.2, max-attacks 16/s and max-attack-packets 20/s. The Speed path is the one that sees Spicy immediately: PacketListener increments totalAttacks for every USE_ENTITY packet regardless of action, and only ATTACK-action C02s increment attackPackets (checked by checkFrequency). Spicy's Hypixel autoblock emits three C02s per blocking cycle (vector INTERACT + INTERACT + ATTACK), so even at the default 10 APS the totalAttacks rate runs ~30/s against the 16/s ceiling -- the module trips (Speed) at default settings the moment a Hypixel blocking fight starts, before any reach argument matters. At 20 APS the ATTACK-only stream alone sits at the 20/s max-attack-packets ceiling. Reach is the second term: the range setting climbs to 6 against max-reach 4.2, so hits beyond 4.2 flag. Direction and NoSwing are the passes: lock mode's -2 degree yaw offset and the upAndDownPitch sweep (bounded at 20 degrees) stay inside the 1.2-radian direction window, and the noSwing option still emits the C0A arm-animation packet, which is what feeds data.lastArmSwing within the 80ms window. The working bypass -- low APS, Hypixel autoblock off, range under 4.2 -- is the reverse of the module's defaults.

countering.label: Reach (combat.reach with interpolation)
countering.explanation:
Grim's Reach is the modern reference for this module (Grim targets current versions, but the geometry it enforces is the same server-side reach the 1.8-era checks approximate). It derives maxReach from the entity-interaction attribute (3.0 base) plus a hitbox margin and a movement allowance, builds the victim box from ReachInterpolationData so the target's possible positions between movement packets are all unioned, fires a ray from the eye position along up to four look candidates (current/last yaw and pitch combinations, since the client's hit-scan can precede the rotation packet), and flags when the minimum distance to the box exceeds maxReach; Reach.threshold defaults to 0.0005 and block-impossible-hits cancels impossible rays. CheckManager lines 112/246 show Reach owning the flag with Hitboxes invoked from inside its verdict.

Spicy's range ceiling of 6 with a default of 4 defeats the check outright: any hit past ~3.1 (attribute 3.0 + margin) fails minDistance > maxReach, and because the module writes its rotation into the same tick's movement packet, all four look candidates resolve to the target direction, so there is no angle confusion to hide behind -- the reach term alone fires. The interpolation union also removes the classic latency dodge of attacking the client-side position of a moving target, since the box covers every server-possible location. The only pass path is range 3.0-3.1, which the module's 0.1-step setting can reach, at the cost of giving up its whole advantage.
